Rising temperatures, shifting population: Changes in children’s ambient heat exposure in China
summary_zh: 研究分析中国儿童环境热暴露变化。提出双重双重分布框架。
summary_en: This study analyzes changes in children's ambient heat exposure in China. Proposes a double-dual-distributional framework.
insights: 创新点：提出双重双重分布框架分析热暴露
方法亮点：考虑地理和时空分布
关键发现：环境热暴露变化显著
insights_en: Novelty: Proposing a double-dual-distributional framework to analyze heat exposure
Method highlight: Considering geographic and temporal distributions
Key finding: Significant changes in ambient heat exposure
abstract: The frequency and intensity of heat waves are increasing, but how these trends translate to changes in the ambient heat to which children are potentially exposed (hereafter, exposures) is not well established. One complicating factor is that it is not only extreme temperatures that change over time, but also the geospatial distribution of children. Another limitation in our understanding is that existing studies often summarize exposure as person-time accumulated above a temperature cutoff, a quantity that confounds the choice of cutoff, the duration of individual exposure, and the share of the population affected. Our study addresses these gaps by developing a double-dual-distributional framework that jointly considers two types of geospatial and temporal distributions (ambient temperatures and child populations) and two types of heat exposure thresholds, namely intensity (heat levels) and duration (hourly exceedance). To illustrate, we assessed potential exposures—the ambient heat conditions experienced—among 250 million children in China, comparing the 1989–1991 and 2019–2021 periods. We found that children’s average annual exposure to moderate or stronger heat increased by 385 h, and the share exposed to strong heat for at least 12% of hours rose from 8.1% (24.9 million) to 23.7% (59.1 million). Both rising temperatures and shifts in child population distributions contribute materially to increased heat exposures in China, a finding that suggests the need for forecasts of children’s potential heat exposures to consider shifting child population distributions.

title: Paradoxical effects of opioids in suppression of colonic motility
summary_zh: 研究揭示阿片类药物抑制结肠运动的作用机制。发现阿片受体激动剂减少肠道神经输入。
summary_en: This study reveals the mechanism of opioids in suppressing colonic motility. Finds that opioid receptor agonists reduce enteric neural inputs.
insights: 创新点：揭示阿片类药物抑制结肠运动机制
方法亮点：研究肠道神经输入变化
关键发现：阿片受体激动剂减少肠道神经输入
insights_en: Novelty: Revealing the mechanism of opioids in suppressing colonic motility
Method highlight: Studying changes in enteric neural inputs
Key finding: Opioid receptor agonists reduce enteric neural inputs
abstract: Opiates slow colonic transit and cause constipation, effects traditionally attributed to suppression of excitatory cholinergic neurons through μ (MOR), δ (DOR), or κ (KOR) opioid receptors on myenteric neurons. However, the cellular mechanisms mediating opioid-induced constipation remain incompletely defined. We found that spontaneous enteric nitrergic motor inputs to mouse colon were reduced by opioid receptor agonists, leading to increased phasic contractions of colonic muscles, an effect abolished by pretreatment with tetrodotoxin, L-NNA, or apamin (in distal colon). Increased contractions in response to opioids are not easily explained by suppression of excitatory neural inputs, and spontaneous cholinergic motor inputs to colon were not suppressed by the MOR agonist Endomorphin-1 (EM-1). Consistent with these effects, MOR were expressed by many nitrergic neurons, and EM-1 reduced the asynchronous activity of nitrergic myenteric neurons during the period of tonic inhibition and the synchronized activity occurring normally just before neurogenic contractions. In addition to increasing phasic contractions, EM-1 enhanced Ca 2+ transients in interstitial cells of Cajal, depolarized membrane potentials of circular muscle cells, effects equivalent to the effects of tetrodotoxin. These are effects consistent with suppression of tonic inhibition. We also found that anterogradely propagating neurogenic contractions in intact colon were suppressed by receptor-specific MOR, DOR, and KOR agonists. Together, these observations demonstrate that opioid agonists suppress inhibitory rather than excitatory motor inputs to colonic muscles. Suppression of inhibitory motor inputs precludes the precisely timed cessation of enteric inhibition that causes poststimulus depolarization and peristaltic contractions.

title: Active immunotherapy against IL-1β restores tissue repair under chronic inflammation
summary_zh: 研究针对IL-1β的主动免疫疗法，加速慢性炎症下的组织修复。使用Coil29纳米纤维，疗法在动物模型中有效，优于单克隆抗体。
summary_en: This study investigates an active immunotherapy against IL-1β to enhance tissue repair in chronic inflammation. The therapy, using Coil29 nanofibers, shows efficacy in animal models and outperforms monoclonal antibodies.
insights: 创新点：Coil29纳米纤维作为IL-1β免疫疗法载体
方法亮点：动物模型验证疗法有效性
关键发现：疗法加速组织修复，优于单抗
insights_en: Novelty: Coil29 nanofibers as a carrier for IL-1β immunotherapy
Method highlight: Validation of therapy efficacy in animal models
Key finding: Therapy accelerates tissue repair, outperforming monoclonal antibodies
abstract: Chronic inflammation driven by sustained interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) signaling disrupts the resolution phase of tissue repair by orchestrating dysregulated immune activity. As a key upstream mediator, IL-1β prolongs the activation of pro-inflammatory myeloid cells and establishes an environment that prevents the transition to tissue repair. Here, we developed an active immunotherapy against IL-1β using the self-assembling peptide nanofiber Coil29, which elicits robust and specific IL-1β-targeted immune responses in both wild-type and diabetic mice, without inducing systemic immunosuppression. In a chronic wound model, the therapy accelerated re-epithelialization and enhanced overall tissue regeneration, outperforming anti-IL-1β monoclonal antibodies. This therapy suppressed macrophage activity, promoted their M2-like polarization, enhanced pro-healing cytokine secretion and enriched the injury site with anti-IL-1β antibodies. In vitro, we found that antibodies from immunized mice reprogrammed M1 macrophages toward an M2-like phenotype, suggesting that antibody-mediated modulation of IL-1β activity may drive the enhanced wound re-epithelization seen in immunized animals. Altogether, these findings highlight a targeted, regenerative therapy for the healing of chronic wounds.

title: Povorcitinib for nonsegmental vitiligo: two randomized, controlled, phase 3 STOP-V trials
summary_zh: Povorcitinib治疗非节段型白癜风，两项3期STOP-V试验显示，52周内显著改善面部色素沉着。
summary_en: Povorcitinib treatment for nonsegmental vitiligo shows significant improvement in facial pigmentation over 52 weeks in two phase 3 STOP-V trials.
insights: 创新点：Povorcitinib作为新型JAK1抑制剂治疗白癜风
方法亮点：双盲随机对照试验验证疗效
关键发现：显著提高F-VASI75评分
insights_en: Novelty: Povorcitinib as a novel JAK1 inhibitor for vitiligo treatment
Method highlight: Double-blind, randomized controlled trials to validate efficacy
Key finding: Significant improvement in F-VASI75 score
abstract: Abstract There is an unmet need for repigmentation therapies for patients with nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV) who are candidates for systemic therapy. Here, 52-week primary results are reported from two parallel phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of once-daily povorcitinib (oral, highly selective JAK1 inhibitor) 30 mg in adults with moderate-to-severe NSV (STOP-V1 and STOP-V2). STOP-V1 and STOP-V2 enrolled 467 and 449 patients, respectively. In both studies, the primary endpoint of ≥75% improvement in the facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (F-VASI75) at week 52 was met, demonstrating statistically significant and clinically meaningful repigmentation with povorcitinib versus placebo (STOP-V1: 18.9% versus 6.8%; odds ratio, 3.1; 95% confidence interval 1.6–5.9; P = 0.0003; STOP-V2: 18.9% versus 3.1%; odds ratio, 7.5; 95% confidence interval 3.0–18.6; P < 0.0001). Povorcitinib was well tolerated; the percentage of patients with any treatment-emergent adverse event (TEAE) was similar between the povorcitinib and placebo groups in both studies (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 68.7%/66.7% versus 63.7%/62.7%). The most common TEAEs with povorcitinib were nasopharyngitis (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 11.2%/11.3% versus placebo, 9.8%/11.1%), acne (10.7%/10.8% versus 3.0%/2.2%) and upper respiratory tract infection (6.9%/14.0% versus 9.0%/10.7%). Serious TEAEs were generally single events, and Janus kinase inhibitor class-specific TEAEs were absent or rare. These results support once-daily povorcitinib as an effective and well-tolerated systemic treatment for adults with moderate-to-severe NSV. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers: NCT06113445 , NCT06113471 .

title: Neoadjuvant botensilimab with or without balstilimab in pMMR and dMMR colon cancer: the phase 2 UNICORN trial
summary_zh: UNICORN试验评估了botensilimab在pMMR和dMMR结直肠癌中的疗效，结果显示botensilimab在pMMR患者中有效。
summary_en: The UNICORN trial evaluates the efficacy of botensilimab in pMMR and dMMR colorectal cancer, showing effectiveness in pMMR patients.
insights: 创新点：botensilimab在结直肠癌中的新应用
方法亮点：多中心临床试验设计
关键发现：botensilimab在pMMR患者中有效
insights_en: Novelty: New application of botensilimab in colorectal cancer
Method highlight: Multi-center clinical trial design
Key finding: Efficacy of botensilimab in pMMR patients
abstract: Preoperative immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are active in patients with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) colon cancer (CC), whereas proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) CC has been consistently considered resistant to first-generation ICIs. In the phase 2 UNICORN trial, we evaluated short-course preoperative botensilimab (BOT; multifunctional Fc-enhanced anti-CTLA-4 monoclonal antibody) alone or in combination with the anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody balstilimab (BOT + BAL) in 56 patients with resectable, locally advanced CC. Twenty-eight patients with pMMR CC were sequentially enrolled in BOT (n = 14) and BOT + BAL (n = 14) cohorts. Twenty-eight patients with dMMR CC followed the same sequential allocation strategy. The primary endpoint of centrally assessed pathological major response (pMR) rate (≤10% of residual viable tumor) was met in all cohorts, except pMMR BOT. Specifically, the pMR rate was 0% (95% confidence interval (CI): 0−23.2%) in pMMR BOT, 36% (95% CI: 12.8−64.9%) in pMMR BOT + BAL, 36% (95% CI: 12.8−64.9%) in dMMR BOT and 100% (95% CI: 76.8−100%) in dMMR BOT + BAL. Secondary endpoints included safety, quality of life, describing treatment-induced transcriptional dynamics, peripheral blood mononuclear cell dynamics, radiomics and radiogenomics features, fecal microbiota composition and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) dynamics. Eight (29%) and 15 (54%) patients treated with BOT and BOT + BAL, respectively, experienced immune-related adverse events, most commonly flu-like syndrome and diarrhea. Single-cell spatial transcriptomic analysis of matched baseline and post-treatment samples highlighted high baseline PD-L1 stromal expression and low post-treatment regulatory T cell signatures in pMMR responders, whereas dMMR responders displayed high baseline FCGR2A and FCGR3A expression on intratumoral macrophages. Clearance of ctDNA before surgery correlated with pathological response and lack of recurrence at data cutoff. Preoperative BOT + BAL elicits pathological responses in patients with pMMR or dMMR CC, supporting the combination as a promising strategy to expand ICI benefits to the early-stage setting. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05845450 . In the phase 2 UNICORN trial, a short course of neoadjuvant botensilimab and balstilimab achieved the primary endpoint of pathological major response rate in patients with pMMR or dMMR colon cancer.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion
summary_zh: 研究旨在确定降低剂量非维生素K口服抗凝剂或阿司匹林是否不劣于双重抗血小板治疗。

insights: 创新点：比较不同抗凝治疗方案
方法亮点：多中心临床试验设计
关键发现：降低剂量抗凝剂与DAPT的疗效比较
insights_en: Novelty: Comparison of different anticoagulation treatment regimens
Method highlight: Multi-center clinical trial design
Key finding: Comparison of efficacy between reduced-dose anticoagulants and DAPT
abstract: Importance Following a left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) procedure, antithrombotic therapy is administered to safely allow time for device endothelialization. However, the optimal postimplant antithrombotic regimen is unknown. Objective To determine if either reduced-dose non–vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) or aspirin alone are noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for the composite clinical end point of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding through 6 months post LAAC. Design, Setting, and Participants This open-label, 3-group, multicenter clinical trial randomized 1857 patients between October 2024 and December 2025 at 87 US investigational sites, with the final 6-month follow-up in July 2026. Enrolled patients had nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, underwent successful LAAC, and were eligible for all 3 regimens. Interventions Patients were randomly allocated 1:1:1 to DAPT for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624), a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613). Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was the 6-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding. Noninferiority was tested in the primary analysis population with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test (α = .025). Bleeding and 45-day device-related thrombus rates were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment. Results The cohort had a mean age of 76 (SD, 8) years, 42.9% were female, the mean CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc score was 4.2 (SD, 1.3), and 68.0% had paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The primary outcome occurred in 41 patients (6.9%) with DAPT vs 31 (5.1%) with a reduced-dose NOAC (risk ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.48-1.18]; risk difference, −1.7 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, 1.2) and 20 (3.3%) with aspirin alone (risk ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.29-0.82]; risk difference, −3.5 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, −0.8). Both monotherapy strategies met noninferiority criteria ( P < .001 for noninferiority for both). Major bleeding was 4.5% with DAPT, 2.7% with reduced-dose NOACs, and 1.7% with aspirin alone; clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was 8.7%, 4.8%, and 3.8%, respectively. Device-related thrombus was observed in 3.4%, 0.9%, and 2.7%, respectively. Conclusions and Relevance Both reduced-dose NOACs and aspirin alone were noninferior to DAPT for 6-month outcomes after uncomplicated LAAC. Method highlight: Combined clinical assessment and metagenomic profiling

abstract: Abstract Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) alleviates climacteric symptoms, but still, microbiome-wide effects and efficacy determinants remain uncharacterized. In this six-month longitudinal study of 356 perimenopausal women receiving oral MHT, we integrated serial clinical assessments with multi-site metagenomic profiling. MHT elicited multi-system estrogenic responses, including neuroendocrine restoration, symptom alleviation, metabolic shifts, and uterine changes. MHT induced site-specific microbiome remodeling, most prominently in vaginal and urinary niches, with moderate oral and minimal gut changes. Generally, MHT reduced Gardnerella vaginalis and increased Lactobacillus crispatus levels in vagina. Baseline vaginal L. crispatus abundance strongly predicted subsequent urogenital restoration. Additionally, baseline urogenital community states stratified therapeutic trajectories: vaginal G. vaginalis-dominated individuals showed transitions toward eubiosis, whereas diversified communities improved less. MHT efficacy corresponded to serum estrogen elevation, linked to baseline gut community type. Individuals with a Phocaeicola vulgatus-driven community type exhibited greater hormonal responsiveness and superior outcomes than those dominated by Prevotella copri. These findings support a precision MHT framework integrating gut community and urogenital typing to guide stratification and targeted interventions.

title: A live biotherapeutic product for adult allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients: a partially randomized, placebo-controlled phase 1b trial

summary_en: Reports the results of a phase 1b trial of SER-155 live biotherapeutic product for the treatment of gastrointestinal microbiome disruption following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant.
insights: 创新点：评估活菌疗法在移植后的应用

abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) microbiome disruption and impaired GI barrier integrity increase the risk of bloodstream infection (BSI) following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant. Here we report results from a two-cohort (open-label, n = 15; randomized, placebo-controlled, n = 45) phase 1b study of SER-155, an investigational, cultivated, multi-strain, oral live biotherapeutic designed to address GI microbiome disruption GI epithelial barrier integrity in allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant recipients. In cohort 2, 34 of 45 participants received either SER-155 treatment (n = 20, SER-155 following microbiome conditioning with oral vancomycin), or placebo (n = 14), and subsequently received transplant. For the primary safety endpoint, SER-155 was well tolerated, with a safety profile comparable to placebo, no treatment-related serious adverse events and no infections with SER-155 species; the most common adverse events were diarrhea and nausea. Four participants in cohort 1 and four participants in cohort 2 (two participants in the SER-155 arm and two in the placebo arm) died during the study; none was attributable to SER-155. For the primary pharmacokinetic endpoint, engraftment was detected for 16 of 16 SER-155 strains, with a median of 11.5 strains detected after the first treatment course. The key secondary efficacy endpoint revealed a significantly lower incidence of BSI with SER-155 versus placebo (10.0% versus 43%; OR 0.15; 95% CI 0.01–1.13; P = 0.0423; 77% relative risk reduction). Other secondary efficacy endpoints (GI infection, acute graft-versus-host disease ≥grade 2, febrile neutropenia and a composite endpoint of BSI, GI infection or acute graft-versus-host disease) were not statistically significant. The secondary pharmacodynamic endpoint of GI domination by Enterococcus and Enterobacteriaceae spp. was not achieved. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04995653 . In a phase 1b study that included an open-label and randomized-controlled cohorts of allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients, treatment with the investigational, cultivated, multi-strain bacterial oral live biotherapeutic product, SER-155, was found to have a similar safety profile to placebo and resulted in fewer bloodstream infections, indicating further clinical investigation of this therapeutic is warranted.

abstract: Amsokigene autoleucel (amsoki-cel, OBX-115) is a tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) cell therapy engineered to express acetazolamide (ACZ)-regulatable membrane-bound interleukin-15, abrogating the need for interleukin-2. In two single-arm trials (completed phase 1 single-center first-in-human (FIH) and ongoing phase 1/2 multicenter Agni-01), patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-resistant advanced melanoma received lymphodepletion and varying doses and schedules of amsoki-cel and ACZ. The primary objective of FIH and Agni-01 phase 1 was safety, tolerability and recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D); the primary objective of Agni-01 phase 2 was objective response rate (ORR) at the RP2D. The first patient treated experienced rapid lymphocyte expansion and vasogenic edema of a previously irradiated brain metastasis, prompting protocol modifications and dose deescalation in FIH, including 80% reduction in maximum amsoki-cel dose and 75% reduction in ACZ dose. After preliminary demonstration of safety at the lower dose, doses were increased in FIH, and reescalation was initiated in Agni-01. Across studies, 37 patients were treated (FIH, n = 17; Agni-01, n = 20). Post hoc pooled analysis demonstrated no dose-limiting toxicities, ICU care or treatment-related mortality. Most common grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) included neutropenia (64.9% (24/37)), leukopenia/lymphopenia (56.8% (21/37) each) and anemia/thrombocytopenia (37.8% (14/37) each). Serious TEAEs were reported for 10 patients, including eight patients with grade 3 or higher events (non-hematologic, 13.5% (5/37); hematologic, 13.5% (5/37)). RP2D was selected based on overall safety and tolerability as well as preliminary anti-tumor activity in Agni-01 phase 1. The phase 2 preliminary ORR was 66.7% (6/9). In total, 15 patients were treated at RP2D and comprise the Key Efficacy Set (Agni-01: phase 1, n = 6; phase 2, n = 9), of which 10 patients (66.7%; 95% confidence interval 38−88%) achieved objective responses (including two complete responses). Amsoki-cel demonstrated favorable safety and promising early clinical activity in patients with ICI-resistant melanoma. A separate phase 2 pivotal Agni-01 cohort is ongoing. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers: NCT05470283 and NCT06060613 . As presented at the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer 2026 Annual Meeting, in a non-prespecified pooled analysis of two trials, amsokigene autoleucel, an autologous tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy engineered to eliminate the need for IL-2, was successfully manufactured and well tolerated and showed a preliminary clinical efficacy signal in patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-refractory melanoma.

abstract: Abstract Aging-related cognitive decline, including impairments in spatial orientation and memory, has been linked to dysfunction within the hippocampus and medial entorhinal cortex (MEC). However, the cellular and molecular alterations underlying MEC aging remain poorly understood. Here we show that old mice exhibit a reduced proportion of grid cells and decreased spatial stability. Transcriptomic profiling of the MEC using 10x Genomics Visium technology reveals 1664 differentially expressed genes between young and old mice. Among these, Bglap3 is identified as a marker gene for a subpopulation of Layer III neurons that showed an age-associated reduction in cell number. Chemogenetic silencing of Bglap3 + neurons in young mice impairs spatial tuning of MEC neurons. Together, these findings elucidate cellular and molecular mechanisms contributing to age-related MEC dysfunction and suggest that the loss of Bglap3 + neurons may underlie spatial coding deficits in aging.

abstract: Abstract Arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), pose a significant global health and economic burden, with Aedes aegypti serving as their primary vector. Arbovirus infection in Ae. aegypti progresses sequentially through the midgut (MG), carcass (CA), and salivary glands (SG), with each tissue exhibiting distinct antiviral responses. Here, we investigate tissue-specific antiviral mechanisms, focusing on the small interfering RNA (siRNA) pathway in SGs. Our results reveal that SGs possess weaker antiviral defense and are more susceptible to arboviral infection compared to MGs and CAs. Notably, overexpression of Dicer2 ( Dcr2 ), a key component of the siRNA pathway, in SGs leads to a significant decrease in arboviral replication. Conversely, Dcr2 overexpression in fat bodies, the primary tissue in CAs, only moderately suppresses DENV2 infection and has no notable effect on Mayaro virus (MAYV) infection. Remarkably, the simultaneous overexpression of Dcr2 in both MGs and SGs enhances antiviral activity, effectively blocking the transmission of multiple arboviruses. These findings reveal the tissue-specific dynamics of mosquito antiviral immunity and underscore the potential for targeting SG-specific immunity to disrupt arbovirus transmission, providing a promising approach for controlling mosquito-borne diseases.

title: Single-cell pharmacogenomic landscapes of epigenetic therapy revealed by gastric cancer Perturb-seq
summary_zh: 研究通过胃癌Perturb-seq揭示了表观遗传疗法的单细胞药基因组学景观，发现了基因剂量与分子表型之间的关系。
summary_en: This study reveals the single-cell pharmacogenomic landscapes of epigenetic therapy through gastric cancer Perturb-seq, identifying the relationship between gene dosage and molecular phenotypes.
insights: 创新点：揭示表观遗传疗法的单细胞药基因组学景观
方法亮点：采用Perturb-seq技术
关键发现：基因剂量与分子表型之间存在关系
insights_en: Novelty: Revealing the single-cell pharmacogenomic landscapes of epigenetic therapy
Method highlight: Using Perturb-seq technology
Key finding: There is a relationship between gene dosage and molecular phenotypes
abstract: Gene expression signatures (“molecular phenotypes”) are extensively utilized in cancer research. To study how gastric cancer molecular phenotypes are regulated by cell-intrinsic genetic alterations interacting with cell-extrinsic therapeutic pressures, we performed direct capture Perturb-seq to interrogate >200 gastric cancer-related genes against 4 distinct epigenetic therapies in normal gastric and gastric cancer lines. We identify 17.7 million pharmocogenomic expression interactions in 625,866 cells representing baseline and post-therapeutic molecular phenotypes. This single-cell pharmacogenomic compendium confirms previously known gene-driven molecular phenotypes, elucidating both poorly characterized genes and gene dosage-molecular phenotype relationships. Molecular phenotypes in post-therapeutic surviving cells capture perturbation-associated pathways associated with drug resistance (epithelial–mesenchymal transition, cell cycle alterations, metabolic reprogramming). Mapping of in vitro molecular phenotypes to primary human gastric cancers uncovers prognostic and spatial variability. Comparative analysis of gene perturbations across therapies and lines reveals both conserved and context-specific molecular alterations. Our results provide a community resource for exploring how Perturb-seq molecular phenotypes are influenced by context dependencies across different drug exposures and cell line backgrounds. Gene expression signatures are widely used in cancer research. This study applies single-cell Perturb-seq to gastric cancer models under epigenetic therapies and reveals gene- and treatment-specific molecular phenotypes and drug-response pathways that have prognostic significance in primary tumours.

title: Microglia-dependent PDGFB regulation of neuronal KCND2 in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus determines propofol anesthesia induction
summary_zh: 研究揭示微胶质PDGFB调控神经元KCND2，影响丙泊酚麻醉诱导。方法为小鼠模型，观察PVN Glu神经元兴奋性。
summary_en: This study identifies a microglia-dependent PDGFB pathway modulating propofol anesthesia sensitivity in mice. Methods involve a mouse model to observe PVN Glu neuron excitability.

abstract: Abstract Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying anesthetic-induced unconsciousness remains a central question in both anesthesia research and neuroscience. However, the role of non-neuronal components in modulating anesthetic sensitivity is poorly understood. In this study, we identify a microglia-dependent platelet-derived growth factor subunit B (PDGFB) signaling pathway that modulates propofol anesthesia sensitivity and contributes to the induction of anesthesia in mice. We demonstrate that PDGFB signaling regulates the potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily D member 2 (KCND2) in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) in mice, thereby orchestrating the excitability of PVN glutamatergic neurons (PVN Glu ) and the activity of their projections to lateral hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons (LH Glu ). Microglia deprivation induces PDGFB deficiency and downregulates KCND2, resulting in PVN hyperexcitability and hyperactivation of the PVN → LH arousal circuit, which contributes to resistance to anesthesia induction in mice. Our findings identified non-neuronal molecular mechanism that governs anesthetic sensitivity, complementing the classical γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor-centric model and providing insights into the regulation of anesthesia induction.

title: Structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference in an infant-derived Bifidobacterium bifidum PNGaseA
summary_zh: 研究婴儿双歧杆菌PNGaseA对N-糖肽的偏好性。方法为生物化学和结构表征，揭示其作用机制。
summary_en: This study characterizes the N-glycopeptide preference of an infant-derived Bifidobacterium bifidum PNGaseA. Methods include biochemical and structural characterization to reveal its mechanism.
insights: 创新点：揭示婴儿双歧杆菌PNGaseA对N-糖肽的特异性。
方法亮点：结合生物化学和结构分析。
关键发现：PNGaseA对N-糖肽有显著偏好。
insights_en: Novelty: The specificity of infant-derived Bifidobacterium bifidum PNGaseA for N-glycopeptides is revealed.
Method highlight: Biochemical and structural analysis are combined.
Key finding: PNGaseA shows a marked preference for N-glycopeptides.
abstract: N-glycans are abundant nutrient sources for human gut bacteria, which deploy peptide: N-glycosidases to release them from glycoproteins. Breast milk is comprised of a high proportion of N-glycosylated bioactive proteins that can be accessed by infant colonic microbes. Here, we biochemically and structurally characterize a PNGaseA-family enzyme from infant-associated Bifidobacterium bifidum LMG13195. This enzyme acts on a broad range of N-glycan structures but shows a marked preference for N-glycans attached to glycopeptides rather than to denatured or native proteins, highlighting a specialized route for N-glycan acquisition in infant-associated Bifidobacterium species. Structures of the apo enzyme, an unliganded E236Q mutant, and a D107N-E236Q complex with a G2-peptide reveal a canonical two-β-sandwich PNGase core plus an additional ten-strand β-sheet cradle and are the first structures of this superfamily. Comparison of these states, combined with molecular dynamics simulations, indicates that glycopeptide binding is coupled to β-sheet cradle-loop movements that close against β-sandwich 1 over the peptide C terminus. The complex defines recognition of the two core GlcNAc residues and the central mannose, reveals that peptide contacts are concentrated around the +2 Thr residue of the NXT sequon, and positions the scissile amide at the active site. These findings, together with mutational and computational analyses, provide a structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference by linking glycopeptide binding to cradle closure and catalysis, thereby expanding the host-glycan nutrient landscape accessible to infant-gut Bifidobacterium species.

title: Genome-anchored foundation model embeddings improve molecular prediction from histology images
summary_zh: 研究通过基因组锚定的基础模型嵌入提高从组织学图像中预测分子特征。方法为PathLUPI模型，在多个任务中评估。
summary_en: This study improves molecular prediction from histology images using genome-anchored foundation model embeddings. Methods involve the PathLUPI model, evaluated across multiple tasks.
insights: 创新点：提出基因组锚定的基础模型嵌入方法。
方法亮点：PathLUPI模型在多个任务中表现优异。
关键发现：PathLUPI在分子预测中优于传统方法。
insights_en: Novelty: A genome-anchored foundation model embedding method is proposed.
Method highlight: The PathLUPI model performs excellently across multiple tasks.
Key finding: PathLUPI outperforms conventional methods in molecular prediction.
abstract: Precision oncology requires accurate molecular insights, yet obtaining these directly from genomics is costly and time-consuming for broad clinical use. Predicting complex molecular features and patient prognosis directly from routine whole-slide images (WSIs) remains a major challenge for current deep learning methods. Here we introduce PathLUPI, which uses transcriptomic privileged information during training to extract genome-anchored histological embeddings, enabling effective molecular prediction using only WSIs at inference. Through extensive evaluation across 49 molecular oncology tasks using 11,361 cases from 20 cohorts, PathLUPI demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional methods trained solely on WSIs. Crucially, it achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of at least 0.80 across 18 biomarker prediction and molecular subtyping tasks, and a concordance index of at least 0.70 across survival cohorts spanning five major cancer types. Moreover, PathLUPI embeddings reveal distinct cellular morphological signatures associated with specific genotypes, whose spatial fidelity is substantiated in representative high-resolution spatial transcriptomics samples. By effectively encoding molecular context to refine WSI representations, PathLUPI offers a strategy to bridge molecular insights with routine pathology workflows for wider clinical application. Obtaining accurate molecular insights for precision oncology remains costly and time consuming. Here, the authors develop PathLUPI, a deep learning method to enable effective molecular prediction in cancer using only routine whole-slide images, with evaluation across 49 molecular oncology tasks in 20 different cohorts.

title: State space models naturally produce time cell and oscillatory behaviors and scale to abstract cognitive functions
summary_zh: 研究提出基于状态空间模型框架，生成类似时间细胞、上升活动和振荡响应的响应轮廓。结果表明，这些行为可从结构化的多时间尺度复杂旋转基中产生，实现优化历史压缩并自然生成结构化时间动态。

abstract: A grand challenge in modern neuroscience is bridging the gap between the microscale neural circuits and cognitive functions. While extensive knowledge exists about neuronal connectivity and biophysics, how low-level phenomena give rise to abstract behaviors remains largely unresolved. Here, we propose that a mathematical framework based on State Space Models offers mathematical sufficiency and computational plausibility to generate response profiles that resemble time cells, ramping activity, and oscillatory responses. Our results suggest that such behaviors can emerge from a structured multi-timescale complex rotational basis, which enables optimized history compression and naturally generates structured temporal dynamics even prior to training, mirroring recent findings in biological circuits. Learning exploits and adapts to the pre-existing temporal basis for specific tasks. We show that the model can readily scale to abstract cognitive functions such as event counting, supporting its use as a computationally tractable framework for understanding neural activities. Understanding how low-level brain circuits support abstract behavior is a longstanding challenge. This study highlights state-space models as a compelling computational framework, showing that they intrinsically produce key neural phenomena such as time cells and oscillations. The framework also scales to cognitive tasks, including temporal discrimination and event counting.

title: Overconsumption of low-digestible sugars can increase susceptibility to Salmonella Typhimurium infection
summary_zh: 研究发现，某些低消化性糖（如阿拉伯糖、乳果糖和聚糖）的过量摄入会降低对沙门氏菌的抵抗力，导致粪便病原体负荷增加和结肠炎。
summary_en: It is found that overconsumption of certain low-digestible sugars, such as arabinose, lactulose, and polyols, can reduce resistance to Salmonella Typhimurium infection, leading to increased fecal pathogen loads and colitis.
insights: 创新点：低消化性糖过量摄入降低沙门氏菌抵抗力
方法亮点：分析低消化性糖对肠道环境的影响
关键发现：发酵导致肠道环境酸化，微生物群失调
insights_en: Novelty: Overconsumption of low-digestible sugars reduces resistance to Salmonella Typhimurium infection
Method highlight: Analysis of the impact of low-digestible sugars on the intestinal environment
Key finding: Fermentation leads to acidification of the intestinal environment and dysbiosis of the microbiota
abstract: Abstract Low-digestible carbohydrates (LDCs), including dietary fibers and sugars that resist absorption, are generally considered beneficial for the gut microbiota. However, we show that acute overconsumption of certain LDCs, particularly low-digestible sugars (LDSs), such as arabinose, lactulose, and polyols commonly used as sugar substitutes, can compromise colonization resistance against the common foodborne pathogen Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium. LDS overconsumption results in elevated fecal pathogen loads, systemic dissemination, and colitis in infected mice. Mechanistic analysis of arabinose overconsumption revealed that rapid fermentation acidifies the intestinal environment, perturbs the microbiota, alters gut-luminal short-chain fatty acid levels and elevated amino acid availability, which can support pathogen growth. Additionally, this perturbation impacts virulence by broadening tissue tropism (e.g. expansion to small intestine) and selecting for invasive Salmonella . Unlike antibiotic perturbations, Salmonella colonization requires SPI-1 and SPI-2 Type-III-secretion systems, linking virulence to pathogen fitness. These findings reveal how dietary perturbations can impact the gut ecosystem in ways that not only compromise colonization resistance but also enhance pathogen virulence.

title: Isoform-resolved spatial transcriptomics on a lab-made high-density array via a single-chip NGS-TGS workflow
summary_zh: 开发低成本高密度芯片进行空间转录组学。单芯片NGS-TGS流程实现全长cDNA分割测序。
summary_en: A low-cost, high-density array for spatial transcriptomics is developed. A single-chip NGS-TGS workflow achieves full-length cDNA splitting and sequencing.
insights: 创新点：低成本高密度芯片实现空间转录组学。
方法亮点：三部分组合长条形码策略解码。
关键发现：识别番茄辣椒嫁接界面相关剪接重编程。
insights_en: Novelty: Low-cost, high-density array for spatial transcriptomics.
Method highlight: Tri-part combinatorial long-barcode strategy for decoding.
Key finding: Identification of interface-associated splicing reprogramming in tomato-pepper grafts.
abstract: Abstract High-resolution spatial transcriptomics is still cost-prohibitive and dominated by short-read sequencing, limiting in situ detection of transcript structures. Here we present a low-cost, lab-made, high-density bead-in-microwell chip assembled by routine centrifuge and decoded by a tri-part combinatorial long-barcode strategy. The design provides 5.6×10 7 barcode combinations across 4.1×10□ capture sites, reducing collisions while remaining tolerant to third-generation sequencing raw errors. Using a single-chip, dual-platform workflow, we split full-length cDNA for next-generation and third-generation sequencing within the same spatial coordinates. In an incompatible tomato-pepper graft, we identified interface-associated splicing reprogramming, including thousands of unannotated isoforms, enriched novel CaGRP1 isoforms, and SlPIP2 intron retention, supported by individual long-read sequences. In mouse embryos, we further demonstrate cross-species applicability by resolving unannotated Col1a2 isoforms in oligodendrocyte progenitors and spatially restricted Dalrd3 intron retention. This cost-efficient system broadens access to spatial full-length transcriptomics and may support diverse biological studies.

title: In vivo ultrasound–MRI 3D mapping of neuromuscular compartments reveals the neuromechanical architecture of finger-specific control
summary_zh: 结合超声和MRI技术揭示手指特定控制的神经肌肉结构。动态超声估计组织运动方向。
summary_en: A multimodal imaging framework combining ultrasound and MRI reveals the neuromechanical architecture of finger-specific control. Dynamic ultrasound estimates tissue movement directions.
insights: 创新点：超声和MRI结合成像技术。
方法亮点：动态超声估计组织运动。
关键发现：生成手指特定控制的3D纤维轨迹。
insights_en: Novelty: Multimodal imaging combining ultrasound and MRI.
Method highlight: Dynamic ultrasound for tissue movement estimation.
Key finding: Generation of 3D fiber trajectories for finger-specific control.
abstract: Abstract Neuromuscular compartments provide the functional substrate for finger-specific motor control, yet their in vivo three-dimensional (3D) architecture remains unresolved because of the absence of clear fascial landmarks for imaging. Here, we present a multimodal imaging framework combining ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to provide volumetric compartment segmentation and in vivo architectural reconstruction of the flexor digitorum superficialis. During isolated finger flexion, tissue movement directions estimated from dynamic ultrasound delineate compartment contours, which are mapped into a 3D MRI reference to generate volumetric compartment masks. Using these masks as constraints, tractography reconstructs 3D fiber trajectories and yields compartment-specific architectural measurements. In ten healthy individuals, compartment topology and fiber orientations were consistent with classic cadaveric anatomy, and estimated compartments accurately predicted surface electromyography amplitude distributions. This framework provides 3D fiber trajectories and quantitative parameters for finger-specific computational models, establishing a foundation for subject-specific neuromuscular digital twins and next-generation neuromuscular interfaces.

title: The CCCH-type zinc-finger PfMD3 promotes translation for malaria parasite transmission
summary_zh: 研究CCCH型锌指蛋白PfMD3在疟原虫传播中的作用。PfMD3与mRNA结合促进雄性配子发育。
summary_en: This study characterizes the role of the CCCH-type zinc-finger protein PfMD3 in malaria parasite transmission. PfMD3 binding to mRNA transcripts promotes male gamete development.
insights: 创新点：CCCH型锌指蛋白PfMD3在疟原虫传播中起关键作用。
方法亮点：研究PfMD3与mRNA结合。
关键发现：PfMD3促进雄性配子发育。
insights_en: Novelty: The CCCH-type zinc-finger protein PfMD3 plays a critical role in malaria parasite transmission.
Method highlight: Study of PfMD3 binding to mRNA transcripts.
Key finding: PfMD3 promotes male gamete development.
abstract: Abstract Sexual maturation and fertility of the malaria-causing parasite, Plasmodium spp., are critical to transmission between hosts. This developmental process involves an intricate gene expression regulatory network that drives gametocyte commitment, development, and the production of male and female gametes. Here, we characterize the role of the CCCH-type zinc-finger protein Plasmodium falciparum Male Development 3 ( Pf MD3) in the formation of gametes. Genetic disruption of Pf MD3 reveals a male fertility defect that decreases infectivity to mosquitoes. Molecular characterization of Pf MD3 reveals its binding to mRNA transcripts is associated with male gamete development through a specific RNA sequence. Gametocyte proteins encoded by these Pf MD3-bound transcripts decrease significantly in Pf MD3 knockout parasites, suggesting that Pf MD3 impacts translation. In addition to RNA-binding, Pf MD3 also interacts with proteins involved in mRNA processing and nuclear export that influence translational regulation. This study establishes Pf MD3 as an RNA-binding protein that impacts lineage-specific translation and male gamete fertility.

title: Visual LLM-guided consensus spatial domain detection with L-STAR
summary_zh: 空间转录组学中，现有方法性能差异大。L-STAR框架利用LLM视觉推理能力，自适应排名和整合方法，实现稳健提升。
summary_en: Existing spatial transcriptomics methods show high variability. The L-STAR framework leverages LLM's visual reasoning to adaptively rank and integrate methods, achieving robust improvement.
insights: 创新点：LLM视觉推理在空间转录组学中的应用
方法亮点：自适应排名和整合方法
关键发现：L-STAR在多个数据集上优于单一方法
insights_en: Novelty: Application of LLM visual reasoning in spatial transcriptomics
Method highlight: Adaptive ranking and integration of methods
Key finding: L-STAR outperforms single methods across diverse datasets
abstract: ABSTRACT Spatial domain detection is a central task in spatial transcriptomics, yet existing methods exhibit highly variable performance across datasets. We introduce L-STAR, a visual LLM-guided, consensus-based framework that leverages the visual reasoning capacity of large language models to adaptively rank and integrate spatial domain detection methods. L-STAR achieves robust and consistently improved performance, outperforming single spatial domain detection methods across diverse datasets.
